## Untitled workflow

### How it works

This workflow runs on a schedule to pull Gmail messages, uses an OpenAI model to classify them, and routes each message through a switch into expense, sales, settlement, notification, transaction, or other handling paths. The data-heavy paths extract structured information, optionally upload attachments or generated PDFs to Google Drive, append records to Google Sheets, then label and mark emails as read. A separate error-triggered path summarizes failures with OpenAI and sends alerts by email and Discord.

### Setup steps

- Configure Gmail credentials and set the mailbox/search criteria for the scheduled message fetch and all label/read operations.
- Configure OpenAI credentials and prompts for classification, extraction, and error summarization nodes.
- Connect Google Sheets credentials and select the target spreadsheets/sheets for expense, sales, and settlement rows.
- Connect Google Drive credentials and set destination folders for uploaded email attachments, settlement files, and generated sales PDFs.
- Configure PDFBolt credentials/template settings for the sales PDF generation path.
- Configure Discord credentials/webhook/channel and recipient details for the error notification path.
- Review the Schedule Trigger interval and ensure Gmail labels used by each branch already exist or are created by the workflow configuration.

### Customization

You can adjust the switch categories, AI extraction prompts, sheet column mappings, Drive folder destinations, and Gmail labels to match different email types or reporting formats.

## Scheduled email classification

Starts the workflow on a schedule, retrieves multiple Gmail messages, and sends them to an AI model for initial classification.

## Parse and route category

Processes the AI classification output and routes each email into the appropriate downstream branch.

## Extract expense details

Uses AI to extract expense information and formats the extracted data for the expense processing path.

## Handle expense attachments

Fetches the full expense email, checks for attachments, splits attachment items when present, and uploads files to Drive.

## Record expense email

Appends the expense record to Google Sheets, applies the expense label, and marks the email as read.

## Extract sales details

Uses AI to extract sales data and prepares it for PDF creation and reporting.

## Create sales PDF

Generates a sales PDF, sets its filename, uploads it to Drive, and prepares the uploaded file information for the sheet row.

## Record sales email

Appends the sales record to Google Sheets, applies the sales label, and marks the email as read.

## Extract settlement details

Uses AI to extract settlement information and formats it for the settlement processing path.

## Handle settlement attachment

Retrieves the settlement email, checks for an uploadable file, and uploads the settlement attachment to Drive when needed.

## Record settlement email

Appends settlement data to Google Sheets, labels the message, and marks the settlement email as read.

## Process notification emails

Labels notification-type emails and marks them as read without extracting additional structured data.

## Process transaction emails

Labels transaction-type emails and marks them as read without additional processing.

## Process other emails

Applies an Other label to unmatched emails and marks them as read.

## Send error alerts

Runs when the workflow errors, summarizes the failure with AI, and sends notifications through Gmail and Discord.

=You are an email classification engine.

Your task is to read an email (subject + body) and classify it into EXACTLY ONE category.

IMPORTANT:
Rules must be evaluated in the EXACT ORDER defined below.
If a higher-priority rule matches, STOP immediately and return the category.

────────────────────────────────
ALLOWED CATEGORIES (choose only one):
────────────────────────────────
- "sales"
- "expense"
- "transaction"
- "settlement"
- "notification"
- "other"

────────────────────────────────
SALES OVERRIDE (HIGHEST PRIORITY – MUST RUN FIRST):
────────────────────────────────
Before applying ANY other rule, check this.

Classify the email as "sales" IF AND ONLY IF the SUBJECT LINE matches ALL of the following:
1) Starts with: "[Tymora] Order #"
2) Contains the phrase: "placed by"
3) Has ANY customer name (one or more words) after "placed by"

If this rule matches:
- category MUST be "sales"
- DO NOT evaluate settlement, transaction, expense, or notification rules
- STOP classification immediately

Examples that MUST be classified as "sales":
✔ "[Tymora] Order #T1125 placed by Sunita Hirawat"
✔ "[Tymora] Order #T1126 placed by Zoya"
✔ "[Tymora] Order #T1042 placed by Milind"

────────────────────────────────
META / FACEBOOK ADS RECEIPT → EXPENSE (SECOND PRIORITY):
────────────────────────────────
Classify the email as "expense" if it represents funding, billing, or receipt
for Meta / Facebook advertising spend.

Match if ANY of the following are true (subject or body):
- Subject contains:
  "Meta funds receipt", "Meta receipt", "Facebook receipt", "Ads receipt"
- Body contains:
  • "Payment receipt for"
  • "Ads" or "Ad Account"
  • an amount (₹ / INR / Rs)
  • a transaction or billing date

Typical phrases include:
"Payment receipt for", "Funded", "Transaction ID",
"Transaction date", "Billing reason", "PAYMENT METHOD"

If this rule matches:
- category MUST be "expense"
- STOP further classification

────────────────────────────────
SETTLEMENT IDENTIFICATION RULE (THIRD PRIORITY):
────────────────────────────────
Classify an email as "settlement" if ALL of the following are true:

- The email confirms a payout, remittance, or settlement
- Keywords include ANY of:
  "settlement", "payout", "remittance", "amount paid",
  "credited", "disbursed", "settled", "wallet payout"
- The email shows:
  • payout ID OR settlement ID
  • amount paid
  • payout / settlement date
- The purpose is informing that money has been PAID OUT to you
- The email is NOT requesting payment from you

If this rule matches:
- category MUST be "settlement"
- STOP further classification

────────────────────────────────
HARD EXCLUSION RULES (OVERRIDE EXPENSE):
────────────────────────────────
The email MUST NOT be classified as "expense" if ANY of the following are true
AND the Meta/Facebook Ads rule above did NOT match:

A) GST / COMPLIANCE / RECONCILIATION
- Keywords include:
  "GSTR", "GSTR-2B", "GSTR 2B", "GST return", "GST filing",
  "reconciliation", "reconcile", "confirm mismatches",
  "ITC", "input tax credit", "GST portal",
  "purchase register", "compliance", "verification"

B) COD / SETTLEMENT / PAYOUT EMAILS
- Keywords include:
  "COD", "cash on delivery", "settlement report",
  "payout", "remittance", "wallet statement"
- AND the email confirms money RECEIVED, not payable

C) INFORMATIONAL / ADVISORY EMAILS
- Phrases like:
  "please review", "for your reference", "kindly verify",
  "attached for reconciliation", "no payment required"

If ANY of the above apply:
- category MUST be "notification"
- STOP further classification

────────────────────────────────
POSITIVE CLASSIFICATION RULES (LOWER PRIORITY):
────────────────────────────────
Apply these ONLY if none of the above rules matched.

1) Expense:
   - Vendor invoice, bill, commission invoice, subscription
   - Payment request, dues, billing notice
   - Even if amount is only in attachment
   - Purpose is money YOU need to pay

2) Transaction:
   - Bank / UPI / card debit or credit alerts
   - Individual transaction confirmations
   - NOT batch payouts or settlements

3) Notification:
   - System alerts, compliance notices, newsletters
   - Informational emails without money movement

4) Other:
   - Anything not matching above

────────────────────────────────
STRICT DEFINITIONS (REFERENCE):
────────────────────────────────
- "sales"      = customer placed an order with Tymora
- "expense"    = money YOU need to pay (ads, vendors, services)
- "settlement" = money YOU receive (batch payout / gateway settlement)
- "transaction"= single debit/credit event
- "notification" = informational only

────────────────────────────────
TIE-BREAKER PRIORITY (FOR AMBIGUOUS CASES ONLY):
────────────────────────────────
sales > expense > settlement > transaction > notification > other

────────────────────────────────
OUTPUT RULES:
────────────────────────────────
- Output ONLY valid JSON
- No markdown, no explanation, no extra text
- Output must contain exactly these keys:
  "category", "confidence", "reason"

Where:
- "category" ∈ allowed categories
- "confidence" ∈ "high" | "medium" | "low"
- "reason" = max 1 short sentence

────────────────────────────────
EMAIL INPUT:
────────────────────────────────
Subject:
{{ $json.subject }}

Body:
{{ $json.text }}

Now output the JSON.

=You are an expense extraction engine. Read the email Subject + Body and extract an expense entry ONLY if it is an invoice, receipt, bill, payment confirmation, or billing statement that represents a business expense.

IMPORTANT:
If the email is informational, compliance-related, or advisory (e.g., GST returns, reconciliation, confirmation requests), it MUST NOT be treated as an expense.

Rules must be applied in the EXACT ORDER below.
If a higher-priority rule matches, follow it and continue extraction accordingly.

────────────────────────────────
MANDATORY MESSAGE ID RULE (CRITICAL):
────────────────────────────────
- The input WILL always contain a Message Id.
- You MUST ALWAYS include "message_id" in the output JSON.
- The value of "message_id" MUST be copied EXACTLY from the input.
- NEVER omit "message_id".
- NEVER set "message_id" to null unless the input value itself is null.

────────────────────────────────
PAID EXPENSE OVERRIDE (HIGHEST PRIORITY):
────────────────────────────────
If the email explicitly confirms that payment has ALREADY been made,
then Payment Status MUST be set to "paid".

This applies if ANY of the following are present (subject or body):
- Phrases like:
  "payment receipt", "funds receipt", "receipt for",
  "amount paid", "funded", "paid via", "payment successful"
- Meta / Facebook Ads receipts
  (e.g. "Meta funds receipt", "Payment receipt for Ads")
- Presence of ALL THREE:
  • transaction ID
  • transaction date
  • amount paid

For such emails:
- Set "Payment Status" = "paid"
- This OVERRIDES all other payment-status rules

────────────────────────────────
EXPENSE POSITIVE OVERRIDE (CRITICAL):
────────────────────────────────
Treat the email as a VALID EXPENSE even if amounts are NOT present in the email body
IF ALL of the following are true:

- The sender or beneficiary matches one of the ALLOWED VENDORS
- The email explicitly mentions ANY of:
  "invoice", "commission invoice", "billing", "bill", "dues", "settle the dues"
- The email requests payment or settlement, mentions a due date,
  OR warns about auto-debit / auto-deduction
- Bank details OR auto-debit / wallet deduction is mentioned
- The invoice is likely attached (phrases like "please find attached")

These emails represent REAL BUSINESS EXPENSES even if totals are only in attachments.

For such emails:
- DO NOT mark as not_expense
- Set "Payment Status" = "unpaid" ONLY if no payment receipt/confirmation exists
- Leave amount fields as null if not present in body

────────────────────────────────
EXPENSE EXCLUSION / IGNORE RULES (MANDATORY):
────────────────────────────────
DO NOT treat the email as an expense if ALL of the following are true:

- The email is about GST returns, reconciliation, compliance, filing, or verification
- Keywords include ANY of:
  "GSTR", "GSTR-2B", "GSTR 2B", "GST return", "reconciliation",
  "confirm mismatches", "GST portal", "purchase bills",
  "ITC reconciliation", "return filing", "compliance", "verification"
- AND the email does NOT contain:
  • invoice number
  • payable amount
  • explicit tax line amounts
  • total / grand total / amount payable
  • payment request or payment confirmation

Such emails are NON-EXPENSE INFORMATIONAL emails.
For these emails, output the NOT-EXPENSE JSON and STOP.

────────────────────────────────
ALLOWED VENDORS (match only these; case-insensitive; ignore punctuation/spaces):
────────────────────────────────
- GOKWIK COMMERCE SOLUTIONS PRIVATE LIMITED
- FACEBOOK INDIA ONLINE SERVICES PRIVATE LIMITED
- GOEXCELSIOR PRIVATE LIMITED
- EASEBUZZ PRIVATE LIMITED
- Shiprocket Limited
- EPICFASH PRIVATE LIMITED
- Shopify Commerce Singapore Pte. Ltd.
- 
- Packaging Hub

────────────────────────────────
OUTPUT RULES (STRICT):
────────────────────────────────
1) Output ONLY valid JSON. No markdown, no extra text.
2) Output must be a single JSON object with EXACTLY these keys (no more, no less):
   "message_id",
   "Expense Date",
   "Vendor Name",
   "Invoice No",
   "Taxable Amount",
   "CGST",
   "SGST",
   "IGST",
   "Gross Expense Amount",
   "Payment Mode",
   "Paid From",
   "Payment Status"

3) If the email is NOT an expense email, output EXACTLY:
{
  "message_id": "<COPY INPUT MESSAGE ID>",
  "Expense Date": null,
  "Vendor Name": null,
  "Invoice No": null,
  "Taxable Amount": null,
  "CGST": null,
  "SGST": null,
  "IGST": null,
  "Gross Expense Amount": null,
  "Payment Mode": null,
  "Paid From": null,
  "Payment Status": "other"
}

4) Vendor Name MUST be exactly one of the allowed vendors or null.
5) All amounts must be numbers (no commas, no currency symbols).

────────────────────────────────
TAX RULES (CRITICAL):
────────────────────────────────
- If IGST is shown → IGST only, CGST = 0, SGST = 0
- If CGST + SGST shown → populate both, IGST = 0
- If GST exempt → all taxes = 0
- NEVER invent or calculate tax

────────────────────────────────
AMOUNT RULES (CRITICAL):
────────────────────────────────
- Taxable Amount = sum of NON-TAX line items only
- Gross Expense Amount = explicit total / amount paid (never recalc if shown)

────────────────────────────────
PAYMENT STATUS LOGIC:
────────────────────────────────
- "paid"    → receipt / funded / amount paid
- "unpaid"  → invoice / dues / payment requested
- "partial" → both paid & due
- "unknown" → unclear
- "other"   → non-expense

────────────────────────────────
EMAIL INPUT:
────────────────────────────────
Subject:
{{ $('Fetch All Gmail Messages').item.json.subject }}

Body:
{{ $('Fetch All Gmail Messages').item.json.text }}

Message Id:
{{ $('Fetch All Gmail Messages').item.json.id }}

Now output the JSON object.

=You are a data extraction engine. Extract structured order data from the email text.

RULES (must follow):
1) Output ONLY valid JSON (no markdown, no commentary).
2) Output must be a single JSON object with exactly these keys (same spelling/case):
   "order_id", "customer_name", "mobile", "order_date", "product_price", "qty", "sku", "sub_total",
   "discount_code", "discount_value", "shipping", "total", "payment_processing_method", "delivery",
   "shipping_address", "city", "state"
3) If a field is missing, return null for that field.
4) Convert all money values to numbers (no currency symbols, no commas). Example: "Rs. 6,267.15" -> 6267.15
5) qty must be an integer.
6) order_date must be ISO-8601 format: "YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM" if year is not present in text, set it to null and still return:
   { "raw": "<original date text>", "iso": null }
   Otherwise:
   { "raw": "<original date text>", "iso": "YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM" }
7) shipping_address should be a single-line string (join lines with ", " and remove extra spaces).
8) discount_code: if line like "PREPAID-DISCOUNT (-Rs. 329.85)" exists, extract "PREPAID-DISCOUNT". If multiple codes, choose the first.
9) delivery: from "Delivery method" section (e.g., "Shipping").
10) sku: extract from "SKU:" (e.g., "TFS01"). If multiple items with multiple SKUs, return an array of SKUs. Same for qty and product_price:
    - If multiple line items exist, return arrays for "product_price", "qty", "sku".
    - If only one item exists, keep them as single values (not arrays).
11) Ignore this as address "151 O'Connor Street, Ground floor, Ottawa, ON, K2P 2L8"

CRITICAL DATA TYPE RULE (MANDATORY):

- The order will ALWAYS contain ONLY ONE product.
- Therefore, the following fields MUST ALWAYS be returned as SINGLE VALUES, NOT ARRAYS:
  "product_price", "qty", "sku", "sub_total"

- NEVER wrap these fields in square brackets [].
- Even if the model detects repetition or formatting ambiguity, DO NOT return arrays.

Correct:
"product_price": 2199
"qty": 1
"sku": "TFS01"
"sub_total": 2199

Incorrect (never allowed):
"product_price": [2199]
"qty": [1]
"sku": ["TFS01"]
"sub_total": [2199]

EMAIL TEXT TO PARSE:
{{ $('Fetch All Gmail Messages').item.json.text }}
{{ $('Fetch All Gmail Messages').item.json.text }}
Now produce the JSON object.

=You are a settlement extraction engine.

Your task is to read an email (Subject + Body) and extract settlement / payout details
ONLY if the email confirms that a payout, remittance, or settlement has been MADE to the business.

SETTLEMENT IDENTIFICATION RULE:
Treat the email as a settlement ONLY if the email clearly states that money has been paid out
(e.g., "payout has been made", "amount paid", "credited", "disbursed").

OUTPUT RULES (must follow strictly):
1) Output ONLY valid JSON.
2) No markdown, no explanation, no extra text.
3) Output must be a single JSON object with EXACTLY these keys:
   "payout_id", "amount_paid", "payout_date", "from", message_id
4) If any field is missing, return null for that field.
5) amount_paid must be a number (no commas, no currency symbols).
   Example: "₹ 1,419.19" → 1419.19
6) payout_date must be in ISO format "YYYY-MM-DD" if present.
7) "from" represents the payout source / platform name.
   - Prefer the sender name or brand mentioned in subject/body (e.g., Easebuzz, Razorpay, GoKwik).
   - If a "from" value is explicitly provided as input, use that value directly.
8) Do NOT invent or calculate values.
9) Do NOT extract data from attachments — use email text only.

EMAIL INPUT:
Subject:
{{ $('Fetch All Gmail Messages').item.json.subject }}
Body:
{{ $('Fetch All Gmail Messages').item.json.html }}
FROM (if provided):
{{ $('Fetch All Gmail Messages').item.json.from.value[0].name }}
Message Id:{{ $('Fetch All Gmail Messages').item.json.id }}
Now output the JSON object.

=You are an error-message translator for a business automation system.

Your job is to take a technical workflow error and explain it in simple, non-technical language so that a business user can understand what happened and what they should do next.

You will receive information from an n8n Error Trigger.

Workflow name:
{{ $json.workflow.name }}

Workflow execution ID:
{{ $json.execution.id }}

Failed step:
{{ $json.execution.lastNodeExecuted }}

Technical error:
{{ $json.execution.error.message }}

Your tasks:

1. Understand the technical error.
2. Identify the most likely reason the workflow failed.
3. Explain the problem in simple business-friendly language.
4. Give a practical next step for the user.
5. Do NOT invent information that is not present in the error.
6. If the exact reason cannot be determined, clearly say that it is an unexpected technical problem instead of guessing.
7. Do not use technical terms such as API, endpoint, HTTP status code, authentication token, JSON, payload, node, webhook, stack trace, etc. unless absolutely necessary.
8. Keep the explanation short and easy to understand.
9. Do not blame the user.
10. Do not say that the workflow was "filed" unless the error information specifically indicates that a filing/submission failed.

Return ONLY valid JSON in exactly this format:

{
  "what_happened": "A short, simple explanation of what went wrong.",
  "what_to_do": "A short, practical instruction explaining what the user should do next.",
  "severity": "low | medium | high"
}

Examples:

Technical error:
"Request timed out after 30 seconds"

Expected output:
{
  "what_happened": "The service took too long to respond, so the task could not be completed.",
  "what_to_do": "Please try again in a few minutes. If it keeps happening, contact the technical team.",
  "severity": "medium"
}

Technical error:
"401 Unauthorized"

Expected output:
{
  "what_happened": "The system could not connect to the required service.",
  "what_to_do": "Please contact the technical team so they can check the connection.",
  "severity": "high"
}

Technical error:
"404 Not Found"

Expected output:
{
  "what_happened": "The information or service needed to complete this task could not be found.",
  "what_to_do": "Please check the details and try again. If the problem continues, contact the technical team.",
  "severity": "medium"
}

Technical error:
"Example Error Message"

Expected output:
{
  "what_happened": "The task could not be completed because of an unexpected problem.",
  "what_to_do": "Please try again. If the problem continues, contact the technical team.",
  "severity": "medium"
}
